name: The Terraces
description:
The Terraces at Palm Creek, Bowling Green Bay National Park, Townsville
Walk leaders - Cherry & Ian
RSVP - Cherry at info@veteducation.com.au
Rating - Grade 5

Short description:
Starting on track this walk quickly becomes off track with rock hopping, steep hills and some scrambling.  This walk starts from private property (no public access).

Important Information:
Pre-registration/approval with the walk leader is essential. Walks are popular, so register early to reserve a spot.

To register or for more info, contact the walk leader info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

Meet point: Contact the walk leader.

Note: The walk starts from private property (no public access).

Fees: Non-members $5.

Walk Description:
The standard Terraces walk starts on track, with the majority being off-track bushwalking and rock hopping. Expect cliffs/ledges, steep hills, loose surfaces, and scrambling.

More information: https://wanderstories.space/the-terraces/

Full day walk. Estimate back at the cars around 4–5 pm.

What to Bring:
- Food/snacks for the day
- Minimum 2 L water (if refilling from creeks, treat properly; otherwise carry 4 L)
- Electrolytes
- Insect repellent (leeches, mozzies)
- Hat, sunscreen
- Personal first aid kit (basic)
- Optional: fingerless gloves, hiking poles (useful in creeks but less so in bush-bashing)
- Clothing & Footwear:
 - Long sleeves or gaiters recommended (off-track terrain may cause cuts/scratches)
 - Sturdy footwear with good grip on slippery rocks

name: White Rock Bay
description:
14th September - White Rock Bay, Cape Cleveland, Townsville
Walk Leader - Molly Hoey
RSVP - Molly Hoey at molly.hoey1@gmail.com

We are going to start by tackling a 4x4 track down coco Creek, across Cape Cleveland, to get as close as possible to the start of the walking section.

Then we are going to walk and climb along the coastline up into White Rock Bay.

The track is about 6 km one way of mixed terrain, and is all off track, so be prepared for mud and spear grass.

Once at the bay we will have a break and explore the beach before heading back along the same track. 

It looks like the weather is heating up quickly so please be prepared for hot weather walking.

Bring at least 3 litres of water, electrolytes, food, sun safe clothing and appropriate closed shoes.

If you have a 4x4 and are experienced taking it off road please let me know other wise we can all car pool.

name: Hermit Falls, Running River
description:
7th September – Hermit Falls, Running River
Leader: Ian Wallace
RSVP: Ian Wallce at ian.wallace@westnet.com.au
Walk Rating: Grade 5

Short Description: 
10 km loop, off-track, thick bush, uneven ground, rock hopping and creek walking. Fit and experienced walkers only.

Important Notice: 
We are attempting to get permits for Mount Spec Road for the day of the walk. Please do not get your own permits unless requested by the walk leader, as this will impact our ability to host the walk.

Walk Description: 
Cross-country woodland, then creek rock hopping and scrambling – no tracks. Terrain includes uneven footing, rock hopping, scrambling, bush bashing, steep climbs, creek walking, some exposed ledges, and long grass. This is a remote area with no facilities and no mobile phone reception.

Cross-country bushwalking to the creek, walk along the creek to Hermit Falls, a wonderful waterfall where we will take a morning tea break and a swim. From the top of the falls, we will walk along the creek and through bush for about 1.5 hours to reach a rapids and gully site for lunch. Then walk cross-country direct to the road, and return along the road back to cars.

Full day walk. Estimate back at the cars around 4:30 pm, ready for the 2+ hour drive back to Townsville.

What to Bring: 
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, minimum 4 litres of water (note this is cattle country: if refilling from the creek, treat well before drinking), long-sleeve clothing and rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), walking poles if required, electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic, if available), personal medications, and sunglasses. Also head torch and whistle.
See also https://wanderstories.space/hermit-falls-paluma/
